## 1

Load in the `Ornstein` data from the `carData` package, along with the `tidyverse` package. Read the help page for the `Ornstein` data to better understand these data.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
data("Ornstein", package = "carData")
```
:::


For today, we will use `interlocks` as the DV, and `sector` and `nation` as IVs. However, we are only interested in whether the nation is Canada or not, so we want to combine the `OTH`, `UK`, and `US` factor levels. One way to accomplish this is to run the following code. (Then use `canada` as an IV instead of `nation`).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
Ornstein <- Ornstein %>%
  mutate(canada = factor(nation == "CAN"))
```
:::


Finally, we will omit data from the "BNK", "CON", and "HLD" levels of `sector` because they have relatively few observations.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
Ornstein <- Ornstein %>%
  filter(!sector %in% c("BNK", "CON", "HLD"), .preserve = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(sector = factor(sector))
```
:::
